meta.title: SecretBar — your agent knows the name, never the value
meta.description: SecretBar keeps passwords, tokens and API keys in the Secure Enclave of your Mac. Your AI agent uses them by name and never sees a value. Command line tool and menu bar app, free and open source.
meta.og_title: SecretBar — your agent knows the name, never the value
meta.og_description: A protocol for secrets and AI agents on macOS: hidden input, Secure Enclave with post-quantum keys, Touch ID, masked output, a Claude Code hook. MIT, no dependencies.
hero.kicker: A protocol for secrets and AI agents · macOS
hero.lede: SecretBar is a command and a menu bar app for the Mac. Passwords, tokens and API keys stay in the Secure Enclave. The agent asks by name, a human confirms, the process gets the value, and the output comes back redacted.
doc.title: Transcript
doc.agent_line: I need the database password for the shop.
doc.note1: The agent sees names and comments. Never values.
doc.note2: Touch ID on your Mac. The value goes into the environment of psql, and nowhere else.
doc.note3: The output comes back masked. Also in base64 and URL encoding.
proto.title: Six rules the value follows.
proto.sub: Every feature of SecretBar enforces one of them. None of them depends on the agent behaving well.
c1.title: Input
c1.text: A human types the value into a hidden macOS dialog: secret ask NAME. The chat never sees it. secret gen makes a random value that nobody sees.
c2.title: Storage
c2.text: Keys in the Secure Enclave seal each value: P-256 and post-quantum ML-KEM-768. The whole file is encrypted again. Nothing goes to a cloud.
c3.title: Access
c3.text: A read needs Touch ID or Apple Watch. The grace time slides for 30 minutes and ends when the screen locks. A lease gives an agent named secrets for up to 24 hours, after one Touch ID.
c4.title: Use
c4.text: secret run puts the value into the environment of one process. Not into argv, a file or the chat. A .env file holds references: secret:NAME.
c5.title: Output
c5.text: Each value in stdout and stderr comes back as ***, also in base64 and URL encoding. A Claude Code hook stops cat .env, secret get and env before they run.
c6.title: Record
c6.text: An access log keeps who read which name and when: agent or human. Names only.
more.title: Also in the box
more.ask: Search by meaning. secret ls --ask "shop database" finds names with the on-device model of macOS 27. It reads names and comments, never values.
more.cookie: Browser sessions. A Safari session moves into the store as a cookie jar. curl uses it, the agent never sees a cookie.
more.gh: GitHub Actions. secret gh NAME -R owner/repo sends a value to gh secret set on stdin, after you confirm.
more.expiry: Expiry and backup. Tokens with a date remind you before they expire. secret export writes one AES-256 file for a new Mac.
more.agents: Any agent. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider: any agent that runs shell commands. Claude Code also gets the hook and ready rules.
app.title: The human side of the protocol.
app.text: ⌥⌘S from any app, Spotlight, Siri and Shortcuts. A card for each secret with the .env files that use it. The app never reads a value: the helper puts it on the clipboard and clears it after 30 seconds.

threat.title: What it stops, and what it does not.
threat.chat_yes: Dialog input, generation, masked output, the hook.
threat.chat_no: A value inside a custom encoding, for example base64(user:pass).
threat.ps_yes: Values go through stdin and file descriptors.
threat.ps_no: secret set NAME VALUE with the value as an argument.
threat.proc: A process reads behind your back
threat.proc_yes: The Secure Enclave key works only after Touch ID or Apple Watch, for any process.
threat.proc_no: Reads inside the grace time: 30 idle minutes, 8 hours at most.
threat.loss_no: Nobody can recover a forgotten backup password.
faq.q1: Does the AI agent ever see the value of a secret?
faq.a1: No. The agent works with names. The value goes into the environment of the command that needs it, and the output comes back with *** in place of the value. A Claude Code hook stops commands that would print a value.
faq.a2: In one encrypted file on your Mac. Keys in the Secure Enclave seal each value. A read needs Touch ID, Apple Watch or the Mac password. Nothing goes to a cloud.
faq.q3: Which AI agents does it work with?
faq.a3: Any agent that runs shell commands: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider and others. Claude Code also gets a hook and ready rules for its CLAUDE.md.
faq.a4: Nothing. SecretBar is open source under the MIT license.
faq.q5: Which macOS version do I need?
faq.a5: macOS 14 or later on a Mac with a Secure Enclave (Apple silicon or T2). The post-quantum store needs macOS 26. Search by meaning needs macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence.
faq.q6: Can I move my secrets to a new Mac?
faq.a6: Yes. secret export writes one file encrypted with AES-256 and your backup password. secret restore reads it on the new Mac.
